indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B3.5.1.1: Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicator.objective: Describe ways of keeping the environment clean

skills.description: Describe ways to keep the environment clean
Explain why keeping the environment clean is important
Identify cleaning tools and materials and their uses
Demonstrate or describe cleaning a specific area safely

misconceptions: Cleaning the environment is only about sweeping.
You can clean without any tools.
Weeding is not part of keeping the environment clean.
Only adults can clean the environment.

questions.stem: Which of these is a way to keep your school environment clean?
options: Leaving empty bottles on the desk
questions.explanation: Sweeping the compound removes dirt and leaves, keeping the environment clean.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think cleaning only happens inside the classroom.

questions.stem: How can you help keep your classroom clean?
options: Eating in class and dropping crumbs
questions.explanation: Putting rubbish in the bin keeps the classroom tidy and prevents pests.
questions.misconception: Pupils may litter if they think someone else will clean it.

questions.stem: Why is it important to keep our environment clean?
questions.explanation: A clean environment reduces germs and pests, helping to prevent sickness.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not connect cleanliness to health.

questions.stem: Which tool is used for sweeping the floor?
hints: You use it on the floor.
questions.explanation: A broom is the tool used for sweeping floors and compounds.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse a broom with a mop.

questions.stem: What should you do with weeds in the school garden?
questions.explanation: Weeding (pulling out unwanted plants) keeps the garden clean and helps crops grow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not consider weeding as cleaning.

questions.stem: Ama is going to dust the shelves. What should she use?
questions.explanation: A duster or clean cloth is used to wipe dust off shelves and surfaces.
questions.misconception: Pupils may use wet tools for dusting.

questions.stem: What happens if rubbish is left to pile up in the school compound?
options: It attracts flies and can cause diseases
It makes the school look beautiful
questions.explanation: Piled-up rubbish rots, attracts flies and pests, and can spread diseases.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize the health hazards of litter.

questions.stem: How can you keep the school toilet clean?
options: Flush after use and wash the floor
Leave dirty water on the floor
Do not clean it at all
questions.explanation: Flushing after use and washing the floor keeps the toilet clean and hygienic.

questions.stem: Why should you wear a nose mask when sweeping a very dusty area?
hints: Dust is bad for your lungs.
A mask covers your nose and mouth.
questions.explanation: Wearing a nose mask protects you from inhaling dust, which can cause coughing or breathing problems.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see the health risk of dust.

questions.stem: Why is a clean environment important for children's health?
options: It reduces the spread of germs and diseases
questions.explanation: A clean environment reduces the presence of germs, which helps prevent diseases in children.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not link environment to health.

questions.stem: Name one way you can keep your home clean.
hints: What do you do with a broom?
What do you do with a mop?
questions.explanation: Sweeping, mopping, dusting, and throwing rubbish in a bin are ways to keep the home clean.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name a non-cleaning activity.

questions.stem: What tool is used for scrubbing the floor?
hints: You use it with soap and water.
questions.explanation: A scrubbing brush is used with soap and water to scrub floors.

questions.stem: How does keeping the environment clean help prevent the spread of diseases?
options: It removes breeding grounds for germs, flies, and mosquitoes
It increases the amount of dust
questions.explanation: Cleaning removes stagnant water and rubbish that mosquitoes and flies use to breed, reducing disease spread.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not understand how diseases spread.

questions.stem: What is the correct way to dispose of rubbish in school?
options: Put it in the bin and empty the bin regularly
Throw it over the school wall
questions.explanation: The correct way is to use a rubbish bin and ensure it is emptied and disposed of properly.
questions.misconception: Pupils may choose unsafe methods like burning inside.

questions.stem: A community organizes a clean-up day. Which of these activities would help keep the environment clean?
options: Sweeping the streets and clearing gutters
hints: Sweeping and clearing gutters remove dirt.
Burning and throwing create more pollution.
questions.explanation: Sweeping streets and clearing gutters removes waste, making the environment cleaner and healthier.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think burning is a good way to clean up.

questions.stem: Ama needs to clean a dusty table. Which tools should she use?
options: A duster and a clean cloth
hints: Dust is best removed with a dry cloth.
You do not need water for dust.
questions.explanation: A duster or clean cloth is appropriate for wiping dust off a table.
questions.misconception: Pupils may use a broom on a table.

questions.stem: Describe the steps you would take to sweep a classroom.

criteria.description: Mentions clearing the floor of items
Mentions sweeping from the corners to the door
Mentions disposing of the dust in a bin

hints: Put the dust in a bin.
questions.explanation: Clearing items, sweeping from corners, and disposing of dust properly are the steps to clean a classroom.

questions.stem: Explain why it is important to keep the school environment clean.

criteria.description: States that it keeps the environment looking neat and free of pests

hints: What happens if it is dirty?
How do you feel in a clean place?
questions.explanation: A clean school environment is safer, healthier, and more pleasant for learning.

questions.stem: Show your teacher how to clean a designated area of the school environment (e.g., sweep a small section of the compound).

criteria.description: Shows proper handling of the tool

questions.explanation: This demonstrates the practical application of cleaning skills.

questions.stem: A school's clean-up club noticed that stagnant water in old cans was breeding mosquitoes. Which action is the BEST solution?
options: Emptying the cans and removing all stagnant water
Adding more water to the cans
hints: Remove the water to stop them.
questions.explanation: Removing stagnant water eliminates mosquito breeding sites, reducing the spread of malaria.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think covering the water is enough.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher two ways you can help keep your community clean.
hints: Think about where you throw rubbish.
questions.explanation: Proper waste disposal and participating in clean-up efforts help keep the community clean.
